scope.summary: This standard specifies the dimensions and structural requirements for two types of mechanical turning arrangements, namely Type A and Type B, used for steel cowl ventilators of nominal sizes 400 mm and above in marine installations.

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Product Specification / Mechanical Dimensions (Marine Outfitting / Ventilator Systems)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Voluntary Engineering Standard (Marine Outfitting / Shipbuilding). Since IS 3276 is an outfitting design standard rather than a safety-critical consumer product, it does not carry a separate mandatory BIS license or ISI certification mark. However, its dimensional tables, tooth distributions, guide roller quantities, and pivot-bearing configurations are universally incorporated in Indian Navy, commercial shipyard, and marine ventilation contract specifications to ensure seamless component interchangeability and smooth turning of ventilation cowls in marine service.

requirements.detail: Materials conforming to this standard and their packages may carry the Standard Mark of the Bureau of Indian Standards (ISI Mark) under the provisions of the BIS Act, indicating structured quality checks by the producer.
Turning arrangements are specified in two standard configurations: Type A (mechanical turning assembly shown in Fig. 1) and Type B (mechanical turning assembly shown in Fig. 2).

requirements.requirement_type: Type B Spur Gear Ring and Drive Pinion
requirements.detail: Type B features a ring, made in two or more sections, with a spur gear cut on its periphery, which is fixed to the intermediate trunking. A driving pinion meshes with this ring and is rotated by a control rod fitted with a handle to facilitate easy turning.
The wheel must be bolted onto the angle iron by countersunk screws. The angle iron is riveted to the intermediate trunking using rivets of 6 mm diameter pitched at 48 mm.

Guide rollers are fitted to the intermediate trunking so the rollers project inwards through the trunking wall. When in position, the roller must maintain a clearance of exactly 2 mm from the ventilator coaming.
The roller bracket must be welded to the intermediate trunking. The roller is secured on the roller pin, which must be fitted with a split pin to prevent the roller pin from jumping out.

requirements.requirement_type: Central Guide Tube and Pivot Bearing
requirements.detail: For large size ventilators, a central guide tube is fitted internally with bearings attached to the intermediate trunking. A pivot rod is attached to the bottom end of the guide tube and bears on a spherically seated washer placed inside the pivot bearing. The pivot bearing is positioned centrally on cross braces welded to the coaming to achieve smooth rotation.
The turning handle assembly must comply with dimensions in Fig. 5 (400 mm total length, 16 mm diameter rod, 22 mm locking sleeve, 20 mm shaft, and 40 mm diameter handle).

plain_language_summary.summary: IS : 3276 - 1966 (Reaffirmed 2022) is the national Indian Standard specifying dimensions and structural layouts for mechanical turning arrangements fitted on steel cowl ventilators used in marine vessels and shipbuilding outfitting. Formulated under the Marine Engineering and Shipbuilding Sectional Committee (EDC 56), this standard defines two distinct turning arrangements—Type A and Type B—for ventilators of nominal sizes 400 mm and above. It establishes precise dimension tables for gear rings (ranging from 42 teeth for 400 mm size up to 134 teeth for 1600 mm size), regulates the quantities of surrounding guide rollers (ranging from 3 to 6 rollers based on size) while enforcing a strict 2 mm operating clearance from the coaming, and outlines detailed internal central guide tubes and pivot-bearings using spherically seated washers to ensure effortless, smooth rotation under harsh sea-going conditions.
